scope: Whole hasher.py, test_hasher.py, root MIT license and pinned _compat.py read. Original hasher imported unchanged with original compatibility helper into isolated namespace.
findings: Short modes base64-encode ASCII hex digest then truncate; mini modes retain three hex digits (12 bits), short modes six hex digits (24 bits), not 24/48 bits suggested by base64 character count.
Original test_hasher checks known vectors for all six algorithms and unknown algorithm errors, but has no collision or file-byte equality assertion.
Compatibility helper encodes Python str using Latin-1, not UTF-8; non-Latin-1 Unicode raises rather than being hashed. Bytes remain unchanged.
none returns empty str while active algorithms return bytes. API does not itself provide exact-file comparison.

control.result: PASS: distinct byte payloads collide under all four truncated modes; full SHA256 differs for each pair. This reproduces weak-key behavior, not an upstream correctness test pass.
